briefs.headline: Alonso rules nobody out of Chelsea's squad for Brentford tonight
briefs.summary: Joao Pedro, who withdrew from Brazil's squad, and Reece James "remain in contention," Xabi Alonso said Thursday, with Moises Caicedo "getting closer." Kickoff at the Gtech is 3 p.m. ET; sixth-place Chelsea lead Brentford by a point.

briefs.headline: Burrow limited a second day; Perine sits out Bengals practice
briefs.summary: Joe Burrow (back) was limited again Thursday and Samaje Perine (knee) did not practice; Shemar Stewart (knee) went full a second day. Houston held Nico Collins (hamstring) and Jadeveon Clowney (knee) out ahead of Sunday's 1 p.m. ET kickoff.

briefs.headline: Dodgers beat the Reds 8-2 as Singer gives up 7 runs
briefs.summary: Kyle Tucker's two-run homer, his 16th, and Max Muncy's two-run double put Los Angeles up 7-0 by the fourth Thursday; Brady Singer (6-15) allowed seven runs in 3 1/3 innings. Sal Stewart hit his 32nd homer as Cincinnati lost the series 2-1.

briefs.headline: Tyson Campbell misses Browns practice with an ankle injury
briefs.summary: The cornerback, who played every snap in the opener, was new to Thursday's report; Teven Jenkins (back) sat out a second day and Dawand Jones went full. Tampa Bay listed Miles Killebrew and Jacob Parrish as limited for Sunday, 1 p.m. ET.

briefs.headline: FC Cincinnati sign 16-year-old goalkeeper Connor Dale as a Homegrown
briefs.summary: Dale, of West Palm Beach, Fla., signed Thursday through 2028-29 and is the club's second-youngest signing; he has seven starts and 37 saves for FC Cincinnati 2 this year. FC Cincinnati plays at Houston on Saturday at 8:30 p.m. ET.

briefs.headline: Del Rio-Wilson and Bausley back atop Marshall's depth chart for Missouri State
briefs.summary: Carlos Del Rio-Wilson and lineman Xavier Bausley, both hurt against Middle Tennessee, are listed as starters for Saturday's 6:30 p.m. ET game in Springfield, Mo., the Herald-Dispatch reported. Cannon Lewis had 14 tackles in Saturday's two-point win over Middle Tennessee.

briefs.headline: Pirates beat the Brewers 7-4 behind a five-run second inning
briefs.summary: Konnor Griffin's two-run double and Oneil Cruz's two-run single chased Kyle Harrison (10-5) in the second Thursday at PNC Park, and Henry Davis' two-run homer in the eighth, his 10th, answered a Milwaukee rally to 5-4. Khristian Curtis won.

briefs.headline: Pochettino names 28 for USMNT friendlies against Peru and Chile
briefs.summary: Thursday's roster has 13 uncapped players and 13 from the World Cup squad, with George Campbell and Yunus Musah back for the first time since 2025. The U.S. plays Peru Sept. 26 in Orlando, 4:30 p.m. ET, and Chile Sept. 29 in St. Louis.

briefs.headline: WVU's defense faces Virginia line averaging 24 years old and 11,000 snaps
briefs.summary: No. 25 Virginia starts two seventh-year and two sixth-year linemen, has allowed two sacks and rushes for 247.5 yards a game, the Dominion Post reported Thursday; WVU's seven sacks tie for sixth in FBS. Kickoff in Charlotte is 7:30 p.m. ET.

briefs.headline: Onosato and six others share the Aki basho lead after Day 6
briefs.summary: Yokozuna (grand champion) Onosato slapped down Gonoyama and ozeki (champion) Kotozakura thrust out Takanosho Friday at Ryogoku Kokugikan; sekiwake (junior champion) Atamifuji, Churanoumi, Asanoyama, Ura and Toshinofuji also stand at five wins and one loss, the Japan Sumo Association's leaders table shows. Nobody in the top division is unbeaten.

briefs.headline: Kirishima's yokozuna bid absorbs a second loss to Yoshinofuji
briefs.summary: The ozeki (champion) had a double inside grip at the edge Friday when No. 2 maegashira (rank-and-file wrestler) Yoshinofuji, winless through five days, threw him over; Kirishima is four wins and two losses. Ozeki Aonishiki, chasing a second straight yusho (championship), was forced out by new sekiwake Fujinokawa, a third straight loss, and is three and three.

briefs.headline: Aonishiki meets Atamifuji on Saturday's Day 7 card at Ryogoku
briefs.summary: Onosato faces Churanoumi, who handed Kotozakura his loss on Day 5; Kotozakura draws Fujiryoga, Kirishima gets Gonoyama, Fujinokawa meets Daieisho and Toshinofuji, the new maegashira (rank-and-file wrestler) at five and one, meets Oho. Hoshoryu, Wakatakakage and Wakanokatsu remain kyujo (absent).

briefs.headline: Bills open new Highmark Stadium by beating the Lions 41-31
briefs.summary: Josh Allen threw for 248 yards and three touchdowns on 20 of 31 and ran for 69 yards and two more Thursday night, and James Cook ran for 135 yards and a score; Jared Goff threw for 327 yards and four touchdowns without an interception. Buffalo is 2-0 under Joe Brady, the first Bills head coach to start his tenure that way, and Detroit is 1-1.

briefs.headline: Bills' DJ Moore leaves the win with a shoulder injury
briefs.summary: Moore landed on his left shoulder reaching for a low end-zone throw in the second half Thursday, was ruled out and walked off for X-rays; Joe Brady had no update afterward. The Vikings placed Jordan Mason on injured reserve Wednesday with a fractured thumb, at least four games, leaving Aaron Jones Sr. as the lead back.

briefs.headline: White Sox beat the Tigers 3-1 and pull even with the idle Guardians
briefs.summary: Chicago held Detroit to one run Thursday at Rate Field and is tied with Cleveland atop the AL Central a day after the Guardians took sole possession; the White Sox host the Tigers again Friday and the Guardians open a home series against the Athletics. Detroit fell six games back.

briefs.headline: Nola's seven innings carry the Phillies past the Mets 3-0
briefs.summary: Aaron Nola allowed three hits over seven innings Thursday at Citi Field, Jhoan Duran earned his 32nd save and Nolan McLean took the loss; Philadelphia is tied with the Cubs for the top National League wild card.

briefs.headline: Crystal Palace and Bournemouth win as the Europa League opens
briefs.summary: Palace beat Lech Poznan 4-0 and Bournemouth won 2-1 at Real Sociedad Thursday on the first league-phase matchday; Ferencvaros won 3-1 at Celtic, Juventus beat NEC Nijmegen 5-0 and Besiktas beat Marseille 4-1.

briefs.headline: Pitt beats Syracuse 27-13 as Angeli is benched after two interceptions
briefs.summary: Steve Angeli was 13 of 25 for 161 yards Thursday night and threw two fourth-quarter interceptions before Amari Odom relieved him; Mason Heintschel ran for 41 yards and a touchdown for Pitt, which led 17-10 at the half. Pitt is 3-0, and Syracuse is 1-2 and 0-2 in the ACC.

sections.label: In Season

coming_in.item: Tomorrow. The migratory bird summary, downloaded and read again this morning, lists Saturday, Sept. 19, and Oct. 31 as the two single youth waterfowl days for ducks, geese, coots, gallinules and mergansers, open to hunters under 18; footnote (b) sets the youth-day bag at the daily limit of the regular duck and goose seasons, except that two scaup may be taken as part of the six-duck daily bag. Hunters under 15 must be accompanied by a licensed adult 18 or older who may not hunt or carry a firearm, only nontoxic shot size T or smaller may be in the hunter's possession, shooting hours are one-half hour before sunrise to sunset, and every licensed hunter needs a HIP registration card. Deed restrictions prohibit all hunting at Warden Lake WMA, and the same table opens the regular duck season Oct. 3-11 at six a day and 18 in possession under footnotes (c) and (d), with coots on the duck dates at 15 and 45.
coming_in.publication: West Virginia Migratory Bird Hunting Regulations Summary, September 2026 - January 2027

coming_in.item: Tomorrow. The second gun window for bear runs Saturday, Sept. 19, through Friday, Sept. 25, in SELECTED COUNTIES, a list the summary table does not carry, so no county is named here; the county-by-county rules and limits are on pamphlet pages 33-39 and vary by permit class, and the bear bag limit is not printed here. Electronic registration is required. The next gun windows are Oct. 3-9 and Oct. 22-25.

coming_in.item: Eight days out. Archery and crossbow seasons for deer and for bear both open Saturday, Sept. 26, and run through Dec. 31, with electronic registration required for each; the deer and bear bag limits are not in the summary table at all, only on pamphlet pages 13-18 and 33-39, and are not printed here. Wild boar archery and crossbow opens the same day, one a season, with registration.

coming_in.item: Fifteen days out, the far edge of this list. The migratory bird summary's next goose date is Saturday, Oct. 3, the first of three splits, five a day and 15 in possession in aggregate under footnote (d), with snow and blue geese on the same dates and limits; ducks, coots and mergansers open the same morning for the Oct. 3-11 first split. Shooting hours are one-half hour before sunrise to sunset, and HIP registration is required. At McClintic and Green Bottom wildlife management areas, waterfowl hours run only until noon Oct. 3-11, the McClintic controlled area is by permit in that window, applied for at WVhunt.com, and concurrent hunting is prohibited there on those dates.

prime.item: Day 7. The general squirrel season opened Saturday, Sept. 12, and runs through Feb. 28, and the summary table sets the daily bag at six and the possession limit at 24, with no season limit and no registration requirement.

prime.item: The first dove segment is in its 18th day with 23 days left after today, running through Oct. 11, with a daily bag of 15 and a possession limit of 45, per the migratory bird summary read again this morning; shooting hours are one-half hour before sunrise to sunset for the rest of the segment, and HIP registration is required. Sora and Virginia rails run Sept. 1 to Nov. 9, 10 a day and 30 in possession in aggregate, and Wilson's snipe Sept. 1 to Dec. 16, eight and 24, on the same table; woodcock does not open until Oct. 17.
prime.publication: West Virginia Migratory Bird Hunting Regulations Summary, September 2026 - January 2027

prime.item: The Marine Fisheries recreational limits page, effective Sept. 2 and opened again this morning, holds red drum at an 18-inch minimum and 27-inch maximum total length, one a day, unlawful to possess over 27 inches. The Fisherman's Post September report, published Sept. 1 and 17 days old with nothing newer on the feed this morning, has Native Son working drum on topwater at docks and creek mouths early and going to deeper, slower jigging or live and cut bait as the sun rises, Speckled Specialist finding reds scattered on oysters, docks, grass points and ledges, Carolina Flats on morning topwater, Spring Tide reporting over-slot schools of 28 to 32 inches that move overnight and river drum early and late, and Jolly Roger Pier taking red drum in the bottom fishing.

Limits page: 14 to 20 inches total length, three a day, one of the three allowed over 26 inches. Speckled Specialist's Sept. 1 paragraph in the Fisherman's Post says trout numbers vary trip to trip with the quality holding, Native Son had them occasional, Jolly Roger Pier had them in the bottom fishing and Surf City Pier early and in the evening; a 17-day-old monthly report, not this morning's water.

Limits page: Spanish 12-inch fork length, 15 a day; bluefish no minimum, and footnote M sets the creel at three per person per day in private recreational fishing and five aboard a for-hire vessel. East Coast Sports' Sept. 1 paragraph had both on casting jigs early and on Clarkspoons trolled nearshore, Jolly Roger Pier had them on plugs and sight casting early and late, Surf City Pier had Spanish on Gotcha plugs and casting jigs, and Spring Tide and South End had bigger Spanish over live bottom and hard bottom in 45 to 50 feet, 17 days ago. King mackerel, which Native Son, Plan 9 and South End expected to fill in, are 24-inch fork length and three a day on the same page.

Limits page: black drum 14-inch minimum and 25-inch maximum total length, 10 a day, one over 25 inches allowed under footnote C; sheepshead 14 inches total length, five a day. The Fisherman's Post Sept. 1 report, 17 days old, has black drum in the bottom fishing at both Jolly Roger and Surf City piers, with pompano, Virginia mullet and croakers, and does not mention sheepshead this month.

sections.label: On the Water

waters.reading: 56.2 cfs, 1.35 feet, falling, five days off the Sunday-evening crest and back at its pre-rain base.
waters.working: Down 2.6 cfs and two-hundredths of a foot from the 58.8 and 1.37 this paper printed at this hour Thursday, and exactly the 56.2 and 1.35 it printed for Sunday morning before the rain, so the river has given back the whole bump. The USGS two-day trace, pulled at 5:37 a.m., runs from 72.9 cfs and 1.47 feet at 5:45 a.m. Wednesday through 60.1 at 1:45 a.m. Thursday, 58.8 at 5:30, 56.2 at 10, 54.9 at noon and 53.7 and 1.33 feet from 2 p.m. to about 8 p.m., the low of the trace, then a small overnight lift to 57.5 and 1.36 around midnight and 56.2 and 1.35 flat from 3:30 to 5:15 this morning. The fetcher's falling flag compares against Wednesday morning's 72.9 and 1.47, the first point of the two-day trace, and it agrees with the 24-hour direction; the trace also shows the river has been within 3 cfs of this number for 20 hours. At base, this is the long-leader, small-fly problem in full: caddis, stoneflies and sculpin are the forage, and pocket water, plunge pools and undercut banks the structure, which at 1.35 feet means a 12-foot leader tapered to 6X, a size 16 to 18 caddis dry or elk-hair emerger drifted through the pocket heads and the tailouts of the plunge pools, a size 16 or 18 stonefly nymph or pheasant tail a foot under it in the seams still carrying current, and a small olive sculpin swung under the undercut banks in the first low light, because at this stage every fish in the pockets can see a shadow on the water. The day is the wet one of the week: NWS Charleston's forecast for Cowen, updated 5:19 a.m., has showers and thunderstorms at an 80% chance, mostly cloudy with a high near 75, a northwest wind of 1 to 5 and a tenth to a quarter of an inch of rain, then a 30% chance before 8 p.m. with a low around 61, and Saturday mostly sunny near 77 with only a slight chance of storms after 5 p.m. A quarter inch on a river at base shows as color at the creek mouths before it shows as flow, and the cloud cover is the one thing in the forecast that helps a wading angler at 1.35 feet.
waters.note: No water temperature came back from the gauge this morning, so no warm-water trout line can be printed. The only NWS product active in West Virginia at 5:37 a.m. was a Special Weather Statement issued 5:08 a.m. by NWS Charleston for a line of strong thunderstorms from southeast of Glouster, Ohio, to near Mason and Rio Grande, moving southeast at 35 mph with gusts to 40 mph, covering Mason, Jackson, Wood and Putnam counties until 6 a.m.; Webster County is not on it. The Monongahela alerts page, opened this morning, carries nothing dated later than Sept. 14 and still lists the July 17 Forest Road 86-Williams River closure and the Aug. 12 Tea Creek Campground construction alert. The fetcher's 24-hour comparison on all three USGS gauges this morning reaches back to Wednesday 5:45 a.m., the first point of the two-day trace; its read string, 'prime wading water', is printed as written.

waters.near: 14 miles above R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam
waters.reading: 25.03 feet, up 0.11 since Thursday morning, climbing off a 24.57 low at 9 p.m.
waters.read: 25.0 ft and rising — normal pool. Ordinary bank access.
waters.working: Up 0.11 over the 24.92 this paper printed at this hour Thursday. The fetcher's 24.71 comparison is Wednesday morning's number, the first point of the two-day trace, but its rising flag is right both ways: the river is up on the day and up 0.46 in the last eight hours. The trace ran 24.98 at 4 a.m. Thursday to a 25.11 top at 11:15 a.m., then eased through the afternoon, 24.93 at 2 p.m., 24.86 at 4, 24.75 at 6, to the two-day low of 24.57 at 9 p.m., and has climbed since, 24.69 at midnight, 24.79 at 2 a.m., 25.00 at 4 and 25.03 at 5, the top of the last 18 hours. The NWPS observation for POPW2 at 5 a.m. is 25.03, matching the USGS figure, and the Weather Service's forecast for Point Pleasant, issued 8:59 a.m. Thursday, had 24.9 at 2 a.m. today and 25.0 at 2 p.m., so the pool is on its curve; action stage is 38 feet and this is normal pool with a little fresh water arriving overnight. Shad, skipjack and crawfish are the forage, and wing dams, riprap, the lock wall and barge cuts the structure: with the pool flat and a few tenths of new water coming down after the overnight storms, the shad are on the upstream faces of the wing dams and off their tips in whatever flow there is, so a white swimbait or a chartreuse-and-white spinnerbait across the faces and off the tips, a black-and-blue jig with a crawfish trailer dragged down the riprap points, and a walking topwater over the barge cuts in the fog, which NWS Charleston's forecast, updated 5:19 a.m., has as areas of fog with showers and thunderstorms likely before 8 a.m. at a 60% chance, fading to patchy fog and a slight chance between 9 and 10, then mostly cloudy with a high near 81 and a north wind of 1 to 7; Friday night is partly cloudy and 61, and Saturday sunny and 84 with an east wind around 2, the fishing day of the weekend on this pool.
waters.note: This is the pool side, 14 miles above R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam; USGS does not gauge the Byrd tailwater. The fetcher's rising flag and read string are printed as written, and the 24-hour direction, up 0.11, is the trace's and agrees with the flag; the fetcher's 24.71 is Wednesday morning's reading, not Thursday's. NWS Charleston's Special Weather Statement, issued 5:08 a.m., puts a line of strong thunderstorms with gusts to 40 mph moving southeast at 35 mph through Point Pleasant, Mason, Ripley and Ravenswood until 6 a.m.; it is the only NWS product active in West Virginia. The NWPS forecast page for POPW2 has the pool at 24.9 to 25.0 through Sunday. The Corps' Huntington District site was not tried this morning and no lock notice is printed.

waters.near: below R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam
waters.reading: 26.05 feet, down 0.43 since Thursday morning, the low of the two-day trace and still dropping.
waters.read: 26.1 ft and falling — normal pool. Ordinary bank access.
waters.working: Down 0.43 from the 26.48 this paper printed at this hour Thursday; the fetcher's 27.23 comparison is Wednesday morning's number, the first point of the two-day trace, and its falling flag agrees with the trace over 24 hours and over every hour since 8 p.m. The river held between 26.47 and 26.68 all day Thursday, the top at 12:15 p.m., sat at 26.53 at 8 p.m. and 26.43 at 10, then fell through the night, 26.31 at 2 a.m., 26.13 at 4 and 26.05 at 5, the lowest point in the two days, with no sign of the overnight bump that lifted it half a foot Wednesday night. The NWPS observation for HNTW2 at 5 a.m. is 26.13, eight-hundredths above the USGS figure, and the Weather Service's forecast for Huntington, issued 8:59 a.m. Thursday, had 26.4 at 2 a.m. today and 26.5 at 2 p.m., so the river is running three to four-tenths under its curve; action stage is 48 feet. Point Pleasant, above the dam, has put on half a foot since 9 p.m., and that water is what will show below the dam later today. With the stage sliding and the pool a foot under Wednesday morning's, the river fishes structure rather than slack: shad and skipjack are the forage, and the seams below the lock wall and off the wing dam tips are where a falling pool concentrates them, so a three-quarter-ounce white swimbait or a skipjack-pattern jerkbait worked along the seam where the eddy meets the flow for hybrids and white bass, and a crawfish-colored football jig dragged down the riprap where the drop is, is the bank cast; the fog before 8 a.m. is the calm water of the day. NWS Charleston's forecast for Huntington, updated 2:34 a.m., has patchy fog and a slight chance of storms before 8 a.m., then showers and thunderstorms likely between 8 and 11 at a 60% chance, mostly cloudy with a high near 86 and a north wind of 0 to 6, a slight chance of storms before 8 p.m. and a low around 64; Saturday is mostly sunny and 88 with an east wind around 2.
waters.note: This is the gauge below R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam, not the tailwater. The fetcher's flag and read string say falling, and the trace agrees on the day, down 0.43 in 24 hours, and on the last nine hours; the fetcher's 27.23 is Wednesday morning's reading, not Thursday's. No NWS product covers Cabell or Wayne counties this morning; the 5:08 a.m. Special Weather Statement for the thunderstorm line names Mason, Jackson, Wood and Putnam. The Corps' Huntington District site was not tried and no lock notice is printed.

waters.reading: Sound at Hampstead: high 1:56 AM at 3.2 ft, low 8:02 AM at 0.9 ft, high 2:31 PM at 4.0 ft, low 9:03 PM at 1.4 ft. Surf at Ocean City Beach pier: high 12:49 AM at 3.4 ft, low 6:39 AM at 1.1 ft, high 1:34 PM at 4.5 ft, low 8:13 PM at 1.5 ft. Water 81.1F at Beaufort, 60 miles up the coast. Moon first quarter, 41% lit, 6.5 days old.
waters.read: Fish the moving water either side of high at 1:56 AM and 2:31 PM in the sound.
waters.working: Neap water: the moon is six and a half days past new, at first quarter by the fetcher's phase, and the quarter is when the sun and moon pull at right angles, so the inlet current is as gentle as it gets in the cycle and the smallest swings run a day or two behind the quarter, into the weekend. The sound swings 3.1 feet from the 8:02 a.m. low to the 2:31 p.m. high, the same range as Thursday, and the ocean station 3.4 feet against 3.7 Thursday and 4.2 Wednesday, so the inlet is softening a notch a day; the afternoon high in the sound holds at 4.0 feet and the evening low at 9:03 p.m. sits a tenth higher than Thursday's at 1.4. The sound today runs 57 minutes behind the inlet on the midday high, 67 on the overnight high, and 83 and 50 minutes behind on the morning and evening lows, so the flood in the backwater runs from 8:02 a.m. to 2:31 p.m. and the afternoon ebb from 2:31 to 9:03 p.m. The 8:02 low is slack, dead water at the inlet, and the first hour of the flood after it is the topwater window Native Son and Carolina Flats both described on Sept. 1, a walking plug along the grass edges and over the oyster bars at docks and creek mouths; as the water tops the bars toward 2:31 p.m., a gold spoon or a paddletail on a quarter-ounce head in the flooded grass, and a live shrimp under a popping cork over the deeper oyster edges and ledges for the trout Speckled Specialist had scattered but of good size, with the gentler neap flood meaning the bait moves less and the cork gets worked slower over the same edges. The last of the ebb, roughly 7 to 9:03 p.m., is the red drum window on the tide preference that matters most here, shrimp and finger mullet draining out of the grass into the creek channels, and a cut mullet or a live finger mullet on a Carolina rig a couple of feet off the channel edge at a creek mouth, the mullet being thick by Carolina Flats' account; Spring Tide's over-slot fish of 28 to 32 inches are over the 27-inch maximum on the limits page and go back. Flounder are closed through Sept. 30 and unlawful to possess: the Carolina Flats one-ounce bucktail with a Gulp curly tail along the ICWW channel edges and dock pilings on the ebb finds them, and they go back too. After dark the flood from 9:03 p.m. pushes bait past the dock lights, and a small paddletail or shrimp imitation drifted through the edge of the light is the trout cast. Surf: the Weather Service's surf zone forecast for Coastal Pender, issued 2:50 a.m., has surf 1 to 3 feet, a LOW rip current risk, no thunderstorm potential, southwest winds 5 to 10, sunny and upper 80s with water in the lower 80s and a high UV index, which is the calm-morning Spanish and bluefish setup from the reference pattern and the one East Coast Sports, Jolly Roger and Surf City reported on Sept. 1: a Gotcha plug or a casting jig under birds off the pier ends on the 6:39 a.m. low and into the flood, with the piers' bottom fishing for black drum, Virginia mullet, pompano and croakers the fallback through the 1:34 p.m. high.
waters.note: The Fisherman's Post Topsail and Sneads Ferry September report is 17 days old, published Tuesday, Sept. 1, at 10 a.m. ET, and the feed, opened at 5:40 a.m., carries nothing newer, so there is no new report; the article was re-opened this morning and it is the month's pattern, not this morning's water. All four sound events and all four surf events fall inside today, midnight to midnight, and the fetcher tagged no spillover on either station. No Beach Hazards Statement is active for Coastal Pender this morning, the second day without one, and the Weather Service had no active alert anywhere in North Carolina at 5:40 a.m. The surf zone forecast gives the Topsail Inlet low as 6:39 a.m. and the high as 1:34 p.m., 57 minutes ahead of the sound's afternoon high; Saturday is a low rip risk with surf 1 to 2 feet, a moderate thunderstorm and waterspout potential and northeast winds around 5 becoming east, and Sunday through Tuesday are low. The National Hurricane Center's 2 a.m. Atlantic outlook has no active systems and one area, AL98, a few hundred miles east of Bermuda, down to 10% in 48 hours and 10% in seven days from 40 and 40 Thursday, with development described as increasingly unlikely as it drifts west over the subtropical Atlantic; nothing near the Carolinas. Hampstead is the sound station and the tide that matters. Water temperature is Beaufort, 60 miles up the coast, not the sound; the surf zone forecast's lower 80s is the Weather Service's own figure for the beach.
